title: Keep your company docs current for your coding agent
summary: Dan Rosenthal's team keeps company knowledge in one repo Claude Code reads; scheduled syncs, human corrections and Claude agents proposing fixes keep it current, with 20+ contributors.
agent_role: Claude agents periodically check the repos for inaccuracies against the team's standard procedures and propose changes; n8n syncs data in on a schedule. A teammate reviews every change before it merges.
outcome: Author reports 20+ non-engineer team members have contributed and says skills improve 3-5x over a few months.
what_they_did: Dan Rosenthal's team keeps everything it knows in one GitHub repo that Claude Code reads each session. n8n pulls in campaign metrics, Slack data and call transcripts on a schedule. Past posts and campaign results are stored in searchable databases. Human corrections become notes, and Claude agents propose fixes that a teammate reviews.
how_it_went: The author says over 20 team members, none traditional engineers, have contributed by writing text files and proposing changes. They report skills get 3-5x better than their first version over a few months.
worth_knowing: The author calls the review step crucial: every change goes through a teammate's review before it applies across the whole company.
prompt: Look through the company knowledge folder in [repo URL] and compare it against our standard procedures in [procedures folder]. Also read the latest synced data in [data folder], such as call notes and campaign results. List any facts that look outdated, contradictory or missing. For each, propose an exact edit and explain why. Put the edits on a new branch and draft a change request for a teammate to review, but do not merge anything.

curation.rationale: Concrete, reusable setup for keeping a company knowledge repo current with scheduled syncs, agent monitoring and reviewed changes; author's account only, but specific tools and steps.
